name: MathlibAnnex.EquivalentSeminorm.nonempty_linearIsometryEquiv_of_pluckerBodies_eq
title: All Plücker bodies determine the norm up to linear isometry

content.display_title: All Plücker bodies determine the norm up to linear isometry
content.one_sentence_role: Recovers a real linear equivalence preserving the two supplied norms.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n=m+1>0$ and $V=\mathbb R^n$ with the reference sup norm and standard Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. The continuous norms $p,q$ have fixed positive comparison constants
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty,\qquad
a_q\|x\|_\infty\le q(x)\le b_q\|x\|_\infty.$$
Set $K_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\}$, $K_q=\{x:q(x)\le1\}$ and $v_p=\lambda(K_p)$, $v_q=\lambda(K_q)$, as positive finite real numbers. For a real linear map $A:V\to\mathbb R^N$, let $A_{ij}=(Ae_j)_i$ be its matrix in the standard bases. The minor-coordinate space has one coordinate for each increasing $n$-tuple $I$ of distinct rows from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and
$$\Pi_n(A)_I=\det(A_{I,*}).$$
Define [the signed generator set](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L19-L24) and [its real convex hull](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L26-L28) by
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal G_p^N
 &=\left\{\sigma v_p\Pi_n(A):\begin{array}{l}
       A:V\to\mathbb R^N\text{ is real linear},\ \sigma\in\{1,-1\},\\
       \|Ax\|_\infty\le p(x)\quad(x\in V)
       \end{array}\right\},\\
\mathcal P_p^N&=\operatorname{conv}_{\mathbb R}\mathcal G_p^N.
\end{aligned}$$
Define $\mathcal G_q^N,\mathcal P_q^N$ in the same way using $q,v_q$. The generators are vectors of minors, not linear maps. Assume $\mathcal P_p^N=\mathcal P_q^N$ for every $N$. There exists a real linear bijection $L:V\to V$ satisfying
$$\forall x\in V,\quad q(Lx)=p(x).$$
content.assumptions: The two norm models and equality of every finite Plücker body are inputs.
content.conclusion: The isometry is between $V$ equipped with $p$ and $V$ equipped with $q$. Preservation of the reference sup norm is not the conclusion.
content.proof_summary: Keep the same limit map and its ball image, recover the norms from positive scaled sublevel sets, and promote that map to a linear equivalence.

proof_steps.text: **Choose the limit map once.** Input the two norm models and body equalities to [limit recovery](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/LimitRecovery.lean#L299-L313). It supplies bijective $L$, contraction, ball inclusion and the exact determinant-volume equation. [ball image equality for that certificate](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/LimitRecovery.lean#L359-L365) gives $L(K_p)=K_q$ for the same $L$.

**Read both gauges from the ball image.** For each $t>0$, homogeneity, linearity and bijectivity give
$$\begin{aligned}
p(x)\le t
&\Longleftrightarrow x/t\in K_p\\
&\Longleftrightarrow L(x/t)\in K_q\\
&\Longleftrightarrow q(Lx)\le t.
\end{aligned}$$
The middle equivalence uses $L(K_p)=K_q$. Its reverse implication also uses injectivity: if $L(x/t)=Ly$ with $y\in K_p$, then $x/t=y$. If the two nonnegative numbers $p(x)$ and $q(Lx)$ differed, their positive midpoint would satisfy one comparison and not the other. Thus $q(Lx)=p(x)$; at $x=0$ both values are zero. The [norm reconstruction from a bijective ball image](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Ball/VolumeRigidity.lean#L185-L212) takes positive definiteness of $p,q$, the real linear bijection and exact ball image as inputs, and returns this equality at each $x$.

**Retain that map in the equivalence.** Bijectivity promotes the same $L$ to a real linear equivalence. Store it and $\forall x,\ q(Lx)=p(x)$ in the two fields of [the model isometry structure](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Module/EquivalentSeminorm/Transport.lean#L76-L79). No sphere restriction is specified by these fields.

content.lean_realization_notes: The recovered equivalence preserves $p$ and $q$ on the same coordinate vectors; it need not preserve the reference sup norm.
